claims.text: Homogenization heat treatments modulate diffusion kinetics in AlCrFeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys.
Modulating diffusion kinetics through homogenization enhances selective oxidation of aluminum.
Enhanced selective oxidation of aluminum produces a continuous and adherent Al2O3 scale.
A continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale protects the alloy against high-temperature oxidation.
As-cast AlCrFeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys have inherently sluggish diffusion.
Homogenization slows the inward diffusion of oxygen.
Homogenization slows the outward diffusion of reactive elements.
The proposed change in atomic mobility favors selective oxidation of aluminum at the alloy surface.
Heat-treated alloys will form a more uniform Al2O3 scale than non-homogenized alloys.
Heat-treated alloys will form a more adherent Al2O3 scale than non-homogenized alloys.
Heat-treated alloys will have lower oxidation rates than non-homogenized alloys.
Heat-treated alloys will exhibit less oxide spallation than non-homogenized alloys.
As-cast AlCrFeCoNi-based alloys typically form less uniform and less adherent oxide scales than homogenized alloys.
As-cast AlCrFeCoNi-based alloys typically have higher oxidation rates and greater spallation than homogenized alloys.
The proposed mechanism applies to AlCrFeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys oxidized at 900–1100 °C under controlled oxygen atmospheres.
Homogenization-induced precipitate formation or grain coarsening could independently affect oxidation behavior.
